title: Inspect and extend: Map validated events to host actions under explicit controls
objective: Use the real implementation in `server/config.js` to demonstrate and safely improve loopback default, bind acknowledgement, port/sensitivity validation, opt-in robotjs, event mapping.
problem: The relay is the boundary that can move the computer. Read configuration before message handling: loopback and logging are defaults, network binding needs explicit acknowledgement, and real input needs its own opt-in. Your implementation or debugging result must remain consistent with the source architecture.
requirements: Read `server/config.js` and the related project files: server/config.js; server/relay.js; server/index.js; server/test/config.test.js.
Add or improve a focused behavior related to loopback default, bind acknowledgement, port/sensitivity validation, opt-in robotjs, event mapping.
Add a meaningful unit test or, when platform tooling is unavailable, document a reproducible manual check.
Update documentation to identify local, simulated, external, and missing behavior accurately.
constraints: Do not claim or implement as complete a capability outside this boundary: There is no TLS or client authentication; network use remains unsafe on untrusted networks.
Do not add credentials, personal records, real funds, or unsafe public network exposure.
Keep the change within the existing project architecture and name any new dependencies.
expected_behavior: The relay is the boundary that can move the computer. Read configuration before message handling: loopback and logging are defaults, network binding needs explicit acknowledgement, and real input needs its own opt-in.
acceptance_criteria: The implementation change is traceable to `server/config.js`.
Normal and failure/edge cases are described and tested.
The test outcome and environment are recorded honestly.
README or source comments correctly state remaining limitations.
hints: Read the caller and the closest existing test before editing.
Separate a pure rule test from any UI, device, provider, or network test.
